user: Explain what a conversion spread means in plain language.
answer:
A conversion spread is the margin the bank adds to the exchange rate when it converts one currency into another.

The market rate you see quoted (the mid-market rate) is the midpoint between buying and selling prices. Verta doesn't give you that rate in full. It adds a percentage on top, so you receive slightly less foreign currency than the market rate would give you. That difference is the spread, and it is how the conversion is priced.

For Tier 1, the spread is 1.5%. It applies only after your free monthly conversion allowance of EUR 500 is used up. Conversions that fit within that allowance carry no spread.

For example, if the spread were applied to a EUR 1,000 conversion, 1.5% of that amount is EUR 15, so you would receive EUR 15 less in value than the mid-market rate gives. This is an illustration only. I don't have your remaining allowance for this month, so I can't say how much of a specific conversion would be charged. A quote for your exact amount will show the rate, spread, allowance applied, and final amount.
